newsitem.title: USA: NYC gains 2,400 jobs in March - city comptroller.
newsitem.headline: NYC gains 2,400 jobs in March - city comptroller.

text.p: New York City gained a seasonally adjusted 2,400 new jobs in March, with 2,900 jobs in the private sector, according to a report released by city Comptroller Alan Hevesi.
Public sector jobs were down 500, according to the report released on Wednesday.
The gain in employment has not kept pace with the increase in the labor force, the report said.
As a result, unemployment climbed to 9.7 percent in March, after adjusting for seasonal fluctuations. Unseasonally adjusted unemployment jumped to 10.1 percent.
The nation's unemployment is 5.2 percent seasonally adjusted, 4.5 points below the city, the highest gap in recorded history, the city comptroller's report said.
For the first three months of 1997, unemployment has been rising, averaging 9.5 percent, up from 8.7 percent in the third quarter and 9.0 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.
In the private sector, construction was up by 2,400 jobs; trade was up by 1,000, including retail with a gain of 200 jobs; and services were up by 1,000.
Strongest sectors within services were: Health up 900 jobs, followed by restaurants up 700, and business services up 400.
Manufacturing was down 1,200 and the financial sector (FIRE) was down by 300, the city comptroller's report said.
In the public sector, local government, which includes city government and agencies such as the Metropolitan Transit Authority, lost 600 jobs on a seasonally adjusted basis.
The Comptroller's Office seasonally adjusts data provided by the New York State Department of Labor.
